details: CONFIRMED for the block: the hook's only skips are stop_hook_active and agent_id (line 72); a headless main session has
neither. I ran the hook with HOME=/Users/amidman on a grader-style PASS line and got the block. The brief promises
"Only the front's reply to the owner"; a headless session's reply goes to a program, and the global rule says "text a tool
or another agent reads keep the project's language (English)". The consequence for each consumer (grader verdict flipped,
max-turns error, extra paid turn per eval session) is PLAUSIBLE until a live run shows it, but the extra rewrite turn on
every headless English reply over 40 letters is certain and repeats on every paid run (principle 2: repeating waste is at
least MEDIUM); the grader breakage makes it HIGH (fails on ordinary use: every paid eval, every bench).
relay already tells program-started sessions apart: lib/relay_transcripts.py:223 treats entrypoint "sdk*" as scripted;
this session's own environment shows CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli for an interactive one.
Size: 15 minutes.

-> {"decision": "block", "reason": "Rewrite the reply in Russian, the owner's native language (only 0% of its words are in Russian); ..."}
find ~/.claude/projects -name '*.jsonl' -mtime -3 | xargs grep -ho '"entrypoint":"[^"]*"' | sort | uniq -c -> 37423 cli, 2788 sdk-cli
measure.py on trial-tally / tmp-repo sessions -> "0% ... 'The trial on tally ... finished'", "0% ... 'The command was blocked before it ran.'"
lib/relay_bench.py:323 llm_grade: claude -p ... --max-turns 1 --tools "" ; verdict must start with PASS
failing_case: front@relay is enabled in ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md says "My native language: Russian.".
lib/relay_bench.py llm_grade runs `claude -p <rubric> --max-turns 1 --tools ""` under that config; the grader answers
"PASS: the reply names the changed file and gives the next step in plain words." The Stop input has no agent_id and no
stop_hook_active, so the hook prints {"decision":"block","reason":"Rewrite the reply in Russian ..."}. The session is
pushed into a second turn (past --max-turns 1, or a Russian rewrite that may not start with PASS), so the grade the
script reads changes. The same happens to every plugin-eval, hooks-live and trial session (entrypoint sdk-cli; 2788 such
transcript entries in the last 3 days, replies like "The command was blocked before it ran ..." at 0% Cyrillic).
Expected: a session started by a program (not the owner) is not checked; nothing printed.
fix_hint: In main(), return early when the session was started by a program: os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT", "").startswith("sdk")
or os.environ.get("RELAY_BENCH"); as a fallback, the transcript's first entry with an "entrypoint" field starting with "sdk"
(the rule relay_transcripts already uses). Add the three tests above to tests/test_reply_language.py.
pass_cases: 1. Stop input {"last_assistant_message": "<the ENGLISH fixture>"} with CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-cli in the environment (or the transcript's entries carrying "entrypoint":"sdk-cli") and native language Russian -> no output, exit 0.
2. Same input with CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli (the owner's interactive session) -> {"decision":"block", ...} as today.
3. Same input with RELAY_BENCH=1 (bench runs set it) -> no output.
4. The Russian fixture in an interactive session -> no output (unchanged).
findings.summary: every headless claude -p session (evals, bench graders, trials) is checked too: its English reply to a script is blocked and rewritten in Russian

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Owner-facing setting with no validation; the brief says the threshold is "60%", so a person is likely to
write 60. Size: 5 minutes.
failing_case: RELAY_REPLY_LANG_SHARE=60 and the RUSSIAN fixture (97%): 0.97 >= 60 is false -> blocked with "only 97% ... in Russian".

findings.summary: RELAY_REPLY_LANG_SHARE=60 (a percent) blocks every reply once; a non-number silently turns the check off

notes: Fine: share of letters, not per character (owner's words met); code fences, inline code, URLs and slash-words removed;
under 40 prose letters skipped; stop_hook_active lets the second stop through; Stop only, not SubagentStop; fails open
(any exception -> exit 0, no output); the language comes from the "My native language:" line relay sync writes; the
script table holds only Russian and Ukrainian. On the live session's 16 replies the check separates the two cases cleanly
(0% vs 94%+), so the 60% threshold has a wide margin. Tests are in a new file, unittest style, and each fails without the hook.
Design remark: the block arrives after the owner has already seen the wrong-language reply; the rewrite is a second
message. That is what was decided (block once), noted only so the owner knows what they will see.
